how.title: Four steps, start to medicine in hand.
how.lede: Nothing to install and nothing to post. If you can open a web page, you can do all of this.
how.bookBody: Choose a clinician and a time that suits you. {clinic} confirms it, and you get a reminder before it starts.
how.payBody: Approve the payment on your phone with MTN or Airtel money. The fee belongs to {clinic}, and you see it before you approve anything.
how.consultBody: Speak to your clinician by video, by voice, or by typing when the network is poor. You choose, and so can they.
how.collectBody: Read your prescription, then collect your medicine from {clinic} or have it brought to you.

care.title: Everything about your visit, in one place.
care.lede: One account at {clinic}, holding the consultation, what was prescribed, where the medicine is, and what you paid.
care.consultBody: Video when the connection is good, voice when it is not, and typing when it is worse. The consultation does not fail because the signal did.
care.prescriptionBody: What was prescribed, how much of it and how to take it — in writing, on your phone, for as long as you need it.
care.deliveryBody: See when your medicine leaves {clinic} and when it is close. The rider is told where to go, never what is in the package.
care.receiptsBody: Every payment you make to {clinic} is receipted and kept, so you can show what you paid and when.
care.familyBody: A parent or guardian can book and consult on behalf of a child, with the consent recorded properly rather than assumed.
care.languageBody: The portal reads in English and Luganda, and you choose which — including the consent you are asked to give.

trust.title: Your clinic. Your records. Your money.
trust.licensedBody: {clinic} is a licensed private clinic and the clinician you speak to is registered to practise. Carevelo provides the software — never the care, and never the diagnosis.
trust.paymentBody: Money moves from you to {clinic}, through the clinic's own mobile money account. Carevelo never holds it, never keeps it for you, and cannot take anything out of your account.
trust.recordsLead: Only your clinic sees your records.
trust.recordsBody: Your consultation notes and prescriptions belong to {clinic} and are visible to the staff there involved in your care. No other clinic using Carevelo can reach them.

faq.title: The things people ask first.
faq.costAnswer: {clinic} sets the price, not Carevelo. You see the consultation fee before you approve any payment, and the price of any medicine before you agree to it. There is no charge for having an account and no subscription to keep it. Your mobile money provider may charge its own transaction fee, as it does for any payment you make.
faq.smartphoneAnswer: Not for all of it. The portal is an ordinary web page, so any phone with a browser can open it to book, to read a prescription and to see what you paid. A video consultation does need a smartphone and a connection that will carry it — and where it will not, the clinician can continue by voice or by typing. If you would rather not use a phone at all, {clinic} can still book you the way it always has.
faq.networkQuestion: What if the network drops in the middle of a consultation?
faq.networkAnswer: The consultation is built to fall back rather than fail: video drops to voice, and voice to typing, without starting again. If you lose the connection completely, open the same link and you return to the same consultation rather than a new one. If it cannot be recovered at all, {clinic} has your number and can reach you.
faq.recordsAnswer: Staff at {clinic} who are involved in your care. No other clinic using Carevelo can reach them: the separation is enforced by the database itself rather than by a setting somebody could get wrong. Carevelo's own staff do not read patient records in the ordinary course of their work — support access is restricted and recorded. Nobody buys your data from us, because we do not sell it and it is not ours to sell.
faq.emailQuestion: What if I do not have an email address?
faq.emailAnswer: Then you cannot use this portal yet, and it is better to say so than to send you round in a circle. Signing in needs an email address and a password, and there is no code-by-text alternative. Ask {clinic} to book you by phone, as you always have — nothing here replaces being able to ring the clinic. If you do set up an email address later, {clinic} can create your account at the front desk and give you a temporary password to change.

Privacy.title: How {clinic} handles your information.
Privacy.lede: What is held about you, who can see it, how long it is kept, and how to ask for a copy or a correction.
Privacy.updated: {clinic} should record the date it adopted this notice, and the date of any change to it.
Privacy.lead: This notice covers the patient portal you are reading it on. It is written by Carevelo, which supplies the software, and it describes what {clinic} does with your information when you use it. {clinic} may hold information about you outside the portal as well — on paper, or in a book at the front desk — and that is covered by whatever the clinic tells you directly.
Privacy.responsibleHeading: Who is responsible for your information
Privacy.controller: {clinic} is. In data protection language the clinic is the data controller: it decides what is collected about you and what happens to it, and it is the one you ask, correct or complain to.
Privacy.processor: Carevelo is the processor. We hold and move the information on the clinic's behalf and on its instructions. We do not decide what happens to it, we do not use it for our own purposes, and we do not sell it — to anyone, for any price. If you ask us directly for your records we will refer you to {clinic}, because it is not ours to hand over.
Privacy.heldIdentity: Who you are. Your name, your phone number, the email address you sign in with, and whatever else {clinic} records to identify you as its patient.
Privacy.heldCare: Your care. Consultations you book and attend, what your clinician records during them, what is prescribed, and what is dispensed or delivered to you.
Privacy.heldPayments: Your payments. What you were charged, what you paid, when, and the reference the mobile money provider returned. Not your PIN, and not your mobile money account credentials — those never reach the portal.
Privacy.heldUsage: How you used the portal. Sign-ins and significant actions are logged, so that unauthorised access to your records can be detected and investigated. That log is a safety measure, not a profile.
Privacy.seenYou: You. Whatever the portal shows you is yours to read for as long as your account exists.
Privacy.seenStaff: Staff at {clinic} involved in your care. Clinicians, pharmacy staff and the people who run the clinic's books see what their work requires.
Privacy.seenNobodyElse: Nobody at another clinic. Every clinic using Carevelo is separated in the database itself, so a clinic that is not yours cannot reach your records even by mistake.
Privacy.seenCarevelo: Carevelo's staff, rarely and on the record. Support and engineering access to live patient data is restricted, requires a reason, and is logged. Nobody here browses records out of curiosity, and there is a record if they try.
Privacy.seenRider: Your delivery rider, and only where to go. A rider bringing medicine to you is given the address and the fact there is a package. Not what is in it, and not why you were prescribed it.
Privacy.paymentsBody: Money moves from you to {clinic} through the clinic's own mobile money account. Carevelo never receives it and never holds it, which also means we never hold the account details it came from — your mobile money provider does, and its own privacy terms cover that.
Privacy.retentionRecords: Your medical records are kept for as long as {clinic} is required to keep them. That period is set by the clinic and by the rules it practises under, not by Carevelo — {clinic} should state its retention period here, and will tell you what it is if you ask. Records are not deleted simply because you stop using the portal: a clinic that destroyed a patient's notes on request would be failing a different obligation.
Privacy.retentionPayments: Payment records are kept for as long as the clinic's accounting and tax obligations require. Sign-in logs are kept for a limited period and then removed.
Privacy.accessHeading: Asking for a copy, or a correction
Privacy.accessBody: You can ask {clinic} for a copy of what it holds about you, and you can ask it to correct anything that is wrong — a misspelled name, the wrong date of birth, a phone number that belongs to somebody else. Ask the clinic directly, using the contact details below.
Privacy.accessNote: A clinical note cannot simply be deleted because you disagree with it, but you can ask for your disagreement to be recorded alongside it. That is the honest position rather than the comfortable one.
Privacy.cookiesBody: Signing in sets one cookie, which is how the portal knows the next page you open is still you. It is not used to follow you anywhere else, and signing out ends it. Choosing a language sets a second cookie holding nothing but en or lg, so the portal opens in the language you chose the next time you visit. Your choice of light or dark theme is kept in your own browser and never sent to us at all. There are no advertising or tracking scripts on this portal, and there cannot be: the site's content security policy refuses to load a script from anywhere but this clinic's own address.
Privacy.wrongBody: Tell {clinic} first — it is the controller, and it can act. If you are not satisfied with the answer you can complain to the authority that supervises data protection in Uganda; {clinic} should name that authority and its address here, along with the person at the clinic who handles these questions.
Privacy.wrongBreach: If a breach affects your information, {clinic} is the one who must tell you. Carevelo's obligation is to tell {clinic}, promptly and in full, and we treat that as a duty to the patient rather than a courtesy to a customer.
Privacy.contactNone: {clinic} has not published contact details in the portal yet. Ask at the clinic, and it can add them here.

Terms.title: Using {clinic}'s patient portal.
Terms.lede: What you can expect from the clinic, what the portal does, and what it is not for.
Terms.updated: {clinic} should record the date it adopted these terms, and the date of any change to them.
Terms.emergency: This portal is not for an emergency. If someone is seriously unwell, bleeding heavily, struggling to breathe, or unconscious, do not wait for a consultation to be booked. Go to the nearest health facility.
Terms.emergencyWithPhone: This portal is not for an emergency. If someone is seriously unwell, bleeding heavily, struggling to breathe, or unconscious, do not wait for a consultation to be booked. Go to the nearest health facility, or call {clinic} on {phone}.
Terms.lead: These terms cover the patient portal — the website you are reading this on. Using it means you accept them. Your care itself is between you and {clinic}, on whatever terms the clinic gives you.
Terms.whoClinic: {clinic} provides the care. It is a licensed private clinic, its clinicians are registered to practise, and every clinical decision — whether to consult, what to prescribe, what to dispense — is theirs.
Terms.whoCarevelo: Carevelo provides the software. We build and run the portal for {clinic}. We do not employ clinicians, we do not review a prescription, and we have no view on your treatment. Nothing on this site is medical advice, and no part of it is a substitute for seeing someone.
Terms.accountPassword: You sign in with an email address and a password. The password is yours and should be known to nobody else — including anyone at {clinic}. If the clinic created your account and gave you a temporary password, the portal asks you to change it before it lets you do anything else, and that is deliberate.
Terms.accountSharedPhone: Handsets get shared in a household. Sign out when you have finished if the phone is not only yours, and tell {clinic} if you think someone else has been in your account.
Terms.accountOnBehalf: Book only for yourself, or for someone you are entitled to act for — your child, or an adult in your care. The portal records who booked and on whose behalf, because a consultation attributed to the wrong person is a clinical risk, not a clerical one.
Terms.bookingBody: A booking is confirmed by {clinic}, not by Carevelo. Cancellation notice, lateness and what happens to a fee if you miss an appointment are the clinic's own policy — {clinic} should state that policy here. Ask at the clinic and it will tell you.
Terms.payingBody: {clinic} sets every price. You see the amount before you approve anything, and you approve it on your own phone with your mobile money provider. The money goes directly to the clinic's own account: Carevelo never receives it and never holds it.
Terms.payingRefunds: That has a consequence worth stating plainly. Carevelo cannot refund you. A refund is {clinic}'s decision and {clinic}'s payment to make, and asking us would only delay it. Your mobile money provider may charge its own transaction fee, which is between you and them.
Terms.prescriptionsBody: A prescription is written by your clinician at {clinic} and dispensed by the clinic. What the portal shows you is a copy of what they wrote, so you can read it at your own pace rather than remember it.
Terms.prescriptionsControlled: Some medicines are controlled and must be collected in person, with identification. Those are never sent out for delivery, by anyone, for any reason. Where delivery is available, {clinic} decides the area it covers and the charge for it.
Terms.unavailableBody: We aim to keep it running and we do not promise it never stops. Networks fail, power fails, and software gets updated. If the portal is down, {clinic} is still there — telephone the clinic, as you would have before any of this existed. Nothing here replaces being able to ring your clinic, and it is not meant to.
Terms.recordsBody: Your consultation notes, prescriptions and receipts are held by {clinic} and are visible to the staff there involved in your care. No other clinic using Carevelo can reach them. <privacy>The privacy notice</privacy> sets out what is held, for how long, and how to ask for a copy.
Terms.endingHeading: Ending your use of the portal
Terms.endingBody: You can stop using the portal at any time and ask {clinic} to close your account. Closing the account does not delete your medical records: the clinic is obliged to keep those for a set period, and it will tell you what that period is.
Terms.endingSuspension: {clinic} may suspend an account that is being used to impersonate somebody, to abuse its staff, or to interfere with the service. Losing access to the portal never means losing your care — the clinic remains reachable by phone and in person.
Terms.changesBody: If these terms change in a way that affects you, {clinic} will make the new version available here and date it. Continuing to use the portal after that means the new version applies.
Terms.lawBody: {clinic} operates in Uganda and answers to the laws and professional regulators that govern private clinics there. {clinic} should state the governing law and how a dispute is to be resolved here; Carevelo cannot state it on the clinic's behalf, and would rather leave a gap the clinic fills than print a clause it never agreed to.
Terms.contactIntro: Questions about your care, a booking, a price or a refund go to {clinic}.
Terms.contactNone: {clinic} has not published contact details in the portal yet — ask at the clinic, and it can add them here.
